_comment: PER-COMPONENT LICENCE REVIEW — the human answer an image scan cannot give.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. scripts/oci-compliance.py determines a corresponding-source
obligation from the LICENCE a component's own metadata records. For Alpine that
metadata is an SPDX expression and the answer is mechanical. For Debian it is a
copyright file: an unordered LIST of every licence appearing anywhere in the
SOURCE package, with no stated relationship between the members and no statement
of which of them govern the BINARY package actually installed in the image. A
scanner cannot tell 'MIT AND GPL-2.0' from 'MIT OR GPL-2.0', so the policy
refuses to guess and lands those components in `manual-review`, failing closed.
THIS FILE IS THAT MANUAL REVIEW, written down. One entry per (component,
version): what the evidence was, what it says, and what follows.
HOW A REVIEW IS MADE. `evidence` names a file the IMAGE ITSELF carries — the
dpkg copyright file at /usr/share/doc/<pkg>/copyright, the Alpine APKBUILD at the
exact aports commit the apk database records, or the apk database record itself —
with its sha256, so the determination can be re-checked against the same bytes.
`governing_licences` are the licences that govern the SHIPPED BINARY, not every
licence in the source tree: where a copyright file's catch-all `Files: *` stanza
is permissive but copyleft stanzas exist, the review says which FILES those cover
and whether this binary package ships them (checked against the package's own
file list in the image).
HOW IT IS CONSUMED. `source_required: false` turns a manual-review component into
`not-required`, with this review recorded in the compliance manifest as the
evidence. `"unclear"` keeps it in manual review. `true` leaves the obligation
standing and the component stays in scripts/source-mirror.json `deferred`.
A REVIEW CANNOT OVERRULE A RESOLVED EXPRESSION. If the scan already resolved a
definite copyleft licence and a review says `source_required: false`, that is a
CONFLICT and the evaluation aborts (exit 2). The review answers questions the
scan could not; it never argues with an answer the scan did reach.
OWNER SIGN-OFF. Every review is `owner_signoff: false` until the owner sets it to
true by editing this file. `scripts/oci-compliance.py --release` refuses to pass
while a review it relied on is unsigned, so an automated first pass can never
clear a production release on its own. `--reviews` prints the counts and every
entry whose `needs_human` is set.
WHAT `reviewer` MEANS. "Claude Fable 5.1 — automated first pass" is exactly that:
a first pass over the evidence, recorded so a human reviews a written argument

WHAT `reviewer` MEANS. "Claude Fable 5.1 — automated first pass" is exactly that:
a first pass over the evidence, recorded so a human reviews a written argument
instead of a hundred copyright files. It is not a legal opinion.

2026-09-06 (tracker 263). netops-correlation moved from python:3.12-slim to
python:3.12-alpine, so the 81 Debian reviews written for that image on 2026-09-05
describe packages no longer shipped and were DELETED with the packages — a review
of bytes nobody distributes is the same rot the register guards against, and
`git show` recovers them if a past release ever has to be re-audited. The two
netops-api Debian reviews and the nine netops-frontend/netops-nginx Alpine reviews
are untouched. Four entries were written in their place: the CPython interpreter at
its new 3.12.14 version (same licence text, byte for byte), and the three Alpine
packages whose licence metadata the scan could not resolve on its own.

reviews.rationale: Alpine's APKBUILD at the aports commit this image records states license="BSD-2-Clause AND custom"; the custom term is the Alliance for Open Media Patent License 1.0, a patent grant. Neither is copyleft.
base-files ships no machine-readable copyright; its free-text copyright states the package is distributed under the GNU GPL 'version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version'.
Alpine's APKBUILD states license="BSD-3-Clause AND IJG AND Zlib" — three notice-only licences.
Alpine's APKBUILD states license="BSD-3-Clause AND BSD-2-Clause AND ISC AND Beerware AND Public Domain" — no copyleft term.

The whole copyright file is four lines: `Files: *  Copyright: public-domain  License: ad-hoc  This package contains public information compiled from around the 'net and many people.` — no copyleft, no source obligation.

Syft's pe-binary-package-cataloger identifies six WINDOWS PE executables vendored inside pip (/usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pip/_vendor/distlib/{t32,t64,t64-arm,w32,w64,w64-arm}.exe) as 'Simple Launcher 1.1.0.14'. They cannot execute in this Linux image and nothing links them, but the image ships NO licence text beside them: pip 25.0.1's own LICENSE.txt covers pip, and pip's _vendor/vendor.txt names 'distlib==0.3.9' without stating distlib's or the launcher stubs' licence. Correlix will not assert a licence it cannot read out of the artifact it ships. The package TYPE this entry is keyed by is a property of the SCANNER, not of the image: Syft's pe-binary-package-cataloger reports these stubs as package type `binary` with no purl, while a run whose dotnet cataloger names them first reports type `nuget` with `pkg:nuget/Simple%20Launcher@1.1.0.14` (the shape the 2026-09-05 inventory was first recorded with). Both spellings describe the same six files, so BOTH are recorded — a scanner-shape difference must never silently drop an undischarged obligation.

Alpine records ONE licence for the whole xz source package, but the xz-libs subpackage ships only liblzma.so.5 (verified against the image's apk database file list) and liblzma is 0BSD upstream — Debian reaches the same determination independently for the same library (liblzma5 copyright, `Files: *` -> 0BSD). The GPL-2.0-or-later term covers the xz shell scripts and the GNU build system, which this subpackage does not ship.

Syft's binary classifier matched /usr/local/bin/python3.12 and /usr/local/lib/libpython3.12.so.1.0 and recorded no licence. The image carries CPython's own licence text at /usr/local/lib/python3.12/LICENSE.txt, which is the PYTHON SOFTWARE FOUNDATION LICENSE VERSION 2 — permissive, notice only. This supersedes the 3.12.13 review of 2026-09-05: the base moved from python:3.12-slim to python:3.12-alpine (tracker 263) and the interpreter version moved with it. The licence text is byte-identical across the two images (same sha256), which is the evidence that only the version changed.

Not a work at all. The apk database record the image carries reads T:'virtual meta package', S:0, I:0, L: empty, and carries NO F:/R: lines — the package installs zero files. It is the `apk add --virtual .python-rundeps` marker the upstream python:3.12-alpine build uses to pin the shared libraries CPython links (its D: line lists so:libbz2, so:libssl, so:libsqlite3 …), each of which is inventoried and evaluated in its own right. A package that distributes no bytes can carry no corresponding-source obligation; the obligation, where there is one, belongs to the packages it depends on.

Alpine's APKBUILD at the aports commit this image records states license="blessing" — the SQLite Blessing, SPDX id `blessing`, which is SQLite's public-domain dedication ('may you do good and not evil'). It is not on this policy's permissive list only because the id is unusual, not because it is unresolved: it grants unlimited use with no reciprocal obligation and no source requirement. The shipped binary is libsqlite3.so.0, built from that same public-domain amalgamation.

The origin package's licence field is a LIST covering the whole xz source tree — 'GPL-2.0-or-later AND 0BSD AND Public-Domain AND LGPL-2.1-or-later' — which is exactly the shape this policy refuses to guess at. The question is what governs the SHIPPED BINARY, and the package's own file list in the image answers it: xz-libs installs R:liblzma.so.5 and R:liblzma.so.5.8.3 and nothing else. Upstream xz states that liblzma is public domain / 0BSD; the GPL-2.0-or-later components are the xz, xzdec and lzmainfo command-line tools and the build scripts, and the LGPL-2.1-or-later component is GNU getopt_long, none of which is in this subpackage. No copyleft work is distributed by xz-libs.

Alpine records this licence as an SPDX EXPRESSION in the apk database the image itself carries (the `L:` field of /lib/apk/db/installed), and the APKBUILD at the aports commit the same database records agrees. The scan therefore RESOLVED it — there is no licence LIST to interpret and nothing for a review to settle. This entry exists to state the obligation in writing, as the register requires, not to reopen it: the Alpine base directory structure and its init scripts are GPL-2.0-only, and Correlix distributes them inside every netops-correlation image.
